principles: Single choke-point: every CLI invocation must pass through one readonly reviewer guard before any handler writes.
Reuse existing command classification instead of hand-maintaining a second mutating command list.
Opt-in isolation only: normal Koala reviewer write lanes remain available unless the caller explicitly sets readonly reviewer mode.
Fail closed and explain recovery: blocked reviewers should return structured findings to the owner, who records authoritative evidence.
drivers: The B-edca incident came from reviewer tool permissions, not from review evidence stale detection itself.
CommandPolicy.ownershipClass already distinguishes readOnly, reviewerWrite, storyScopedMutating, mainSharedMutating, and dangerousMutating.
Koala needs to support both advisory external reviewers and normal gate-writing reviewers without conflating them.

options.name: env-gated-readonly-choke-point
pros: Can be injected at spawn time for Claude/Codex/Gemini CLI without changing every reviewer command schema
Uses resolveEffectiveOwnershipClass so new mutating commands are automatically blocked unless classified readOnly
Preserves normal reviewerWrite path when the env var is absent
cons: Owner must remember to set the env var for advisory external reviewers
If the env leaks into a normal reviewer process, legitimate reviewer evidence writes are blocked with a clear error

options.name: per-command-allowlist
pros: Very explicit list of blocked commands
Could show a tailored error per command
cons: High drift risk whenever Koala adds commands
Likely to miss reviewerWrite or mainSharedMutating edge cases

options.name: tool-permission-only
pros: No Koala code change if every launcher perfectly restricts Bash
cons: Already failed in practice when a read-only reviewer got Bash
Cannot protect unknown future launchers or manual CLI use

rationale: Use KOALA_REVIEWER_READONLY=1 as an explicit spawn-time/read-only reviewer signal and enforce it in cli-engine.ts before hooks and before handlers. The guard will allow only effective ownershipClass=readOnly commands and block reviewerWrite, storyScopedMutating, mainSharedMutating, dangerousMutating, and unclassified commands. This directly closes the advisory reviewer write hole without weakening normal signed reviewer lanes.

preMortem.scenario: Readonly env leaks into a normal gate reviewer
preMortem.trigger: Owner exports KOALA_REVIEWER_READONLY globally instead of setting it only on an advisory reviewer command
preMortem.consequence: Normal review_run_start/review_pass_set fails and REVIEW cannot progress
preMortem.mitigation: Make the error name KOALA_REVIEWER_READONLY and docs say set it only per spawned advisory process; tests prove normal no-env reviewerWrite still passes

preMortem.scenario: A new mutating command bypasses readonly mode
preMortem.trigger: Future command is added and classified reviewerWrite/mainSharedMutating/storyScopedMutating but the readonly guard uses a stale hand-written block list
preMortem.consequence: Advisory reviewer can still mutate state
preMortem.mitigation: Guard uses resolveEffectiveOwnershipClass and allows only readOnly; command-ownership contract covers all MAIN_TOOLS classification

preMortem.scenario: Blocked command still triggers hooks or partial writes
preMortem.trigger: Readonly guard runs after preCommand hooks or inside an individual handler
preMortem.consequence: A rejected advisory reviewer still leaves side effects
preMortem.mitigation: Run readonly guard in cli-engine.ts before preCommand hooks and before enforceStoryOwnerLeaseGate/handler invocation; smoke test asserts blocked command produces no review pass artifact

preMortem.scenario: Readonly mode conflicts with owner takeover semantics
preMortem.consequence: Reviewer seizes ownership despite intended read-only role
preMortem.mitigation: Readonly guard checks effective class before owner lease/takeover flow, so dangerousMutating/storyScopedMutating commands are blocked regardless of takeover flags
